title: Have you seen this domino (Re-upload)
author: Hempelson Tamsova
rules:
This is a reupload of the first puzzle I ever made. It has barely gotten any solves (even on SudokuPad), which I don't mind generally speaking, though I was curious about why that might be. Now that it's been almost a month and the solution wasn't too fresh in my mind, I was able to test-solve it as if I weren't the author. The only major issue I spotted was the ruleset, so I made a few visual adjustments, rephrased the rules, and decided to give it a second try. I'm still not sure if a 3-star difficulty rating is too low or too high, though.

Normal Sudoku rules apply.

In every row, the digits of each set ({1,4,7},{2,5,8},{3,6,9}) must form a horizontally contiguous block of three cells.

• Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. All possible white dots are given.
• Digits separated by a black dot contain digits in a 1:2 ratio. Exactly 6 black dots (dominoes) are missing.
(No white dot is hidden beneath a black dot and vice versa)

There are 3 sets of 3 squares (9 squares total), which together contain one complete set of the digits 1–9. Squares within the same set have an identical appearance.

In each set of 3, two squares each see strictly one single cell belonging to a missing black-dot domino within their 3x3 neighborhood (a chess King's move), while the third square sees none.

No square sees more than one missing domino, and no missing domino is seen by more than one square (creating a 1-to-1 match between the 6 "seeing" squares and the 6 missing dominoes).

• Example: Suppose there is a set of 3 dotted squares. One dotted
square (A) sees a single cell of missing domino 1, and a second dotted
square (B) sees a single cell of missing domino 2.
Neither A nor B sees any other missing domino, and no other square in the grid sees domino 1 or 2.
The third dotted square (C) does not see any cell of any missing domino.

• Note: A square's 3x3 neighborhood cannot touch both cells of a missing domino. However, a square may be part of a missing domino itself, as it only touches its partner cell.

solve with SudokuPad
solutionCode: the diagonal (top left corner to bottom right, 9 digits, no spaces in between)
